mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact the S&P 500 over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5.5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If unemployment exceeds 5.5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate is above 3%, it indicates tight monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 3% but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high federal funds rate and low unemployment rate indicates a strong economy but potential inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in payroll employment growth signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If payroll growth slows but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production combined with strong GDP growth indicates supply chain issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If industrial production lags GDP growth but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail sales indicates weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If retail sales decline but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 40% of the time.
